page: Amazon Web Services x8i.metal-48xl is a bare-metal, memory-optimized server powered by Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors. It features 192 vCPUs across 96 physical cores with a dedicated allocation and a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, supported by a massive 480 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 3072.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, providing 16.0 GB of RAM per core. The server does not include local storage or GPUs, but it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 75 Gbps.

In benchmark testing, the x8i.metal-48xl demonstrates top-tier multi-core performance, scoring in the top 10% for stress-ng multi-core CPU tests and Geekbench multi-core metrics. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, with read-only cached small block speeds reaching 15496.43 GB/sec and uncached large block speeds at 525.98 GB/sec, both ranking in the top 10%. However, single-core CPU performance and Passmark memory scores fall into the average category. The CPU features advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), which drive top-tier performance in LLM prompt processing and cryptography.

Given its bare-metal nature and massive memory footprint, this server offers high resource density for memory-intensive enterprise workloads. It is highly cost-efficient for large-scale operations that can fully utilize its 3 TB of DDR5 RAM and 192 vCPUs, though the lack of bundled local storage requires external network-attached storage solutions. The server is highly suited for large in-memory databases, Redis deployments, software compilation, and heavy multi-threaded workloads such as LLM inference prompt processing and data-dense enterprise applications.
